1: Every day follows the same order: understand the concepts and their examples, then build by hand, copy and try the code, memorize the terms, and finish with a challenge and a quiz. Don't move to the next day until you answer at least 4 of the 5 questions in the day's quiz correctly.
8: 12 weeks, and every week has two tracks running side by side: n8n (the tool) and a language (what you need to control the tool). Click any week to open its daily plan below.
13: Tip: Don't learn a language in a vacuum. Every time you learn something new, use it in a real workflow the same day — Regex to clean a phone number, Python to call an API. What you use sticks; what you only read gets forgotten.
14: Start with the intensive week: 7 days, about 3 hours a day, covering the most important things you'll use in n8n. Then continue with the full plan (12 weeks) to lock in the languages (Python, JavaScript, SQL and more) and build a portfolio.
